text:
Predicates:
TwinsOrTriplets(x) ::: x is a twin or triplet.
SiblingsSameAge(x) ::: x has siblings who are the same age.
ComplainOften(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHome(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
StrongBonds(x) ::: x develops strong bonds with their family members.
Premises:
(TwinsOrTriplets(x) ∨ TwinsOrTriplets(x)) → (∃y (Sibling(x, y) ∧ SpendTime(x, y))) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
SiblingsSameAge(x) → (TwinsOrTriplets(x) ∨ TwinsOrTriplets(x)) ::: If people have siblings who are the same age, then they are twins or triplets.
ComplainOften(x) → SiblingsSameAge(x) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who are the same age.
¬LiveAtHome(x) → ¬StrongBonds(x) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds with their family members.
SpendTime(x, y) → ¬LiveAtHome(x) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings, then they often did not live at home regularly.
(TwinsOrTriplets(luke) ∧ StrongBonds(luke)) ⊕ ¬(TwinsOrTriplets(luke) ∨ StrongBonds(luke)) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds with his family members, or he neither is a twin or triplet nor develops strong bonds with his family members.
Conclusion:
ComplainOften(luke) ::: Luke complains often about annoying siblings.
